introduction_markdown:
Physics 1, Ordinary Level, June 2019 (0580). Multiple choice paper, one and a half hours. Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; choose the best one. Section 1 (Questions 1 to 43) has separate questions; Section 2 (Questions 44 to 50) groups questions on practical situations. Non-programmable and cordless calculators are allowed. Useful constants: acceleration of free fall $g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; speed of light in vacuum $c = 3\times 10^{8}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; charge on an electron $e = 1.6\times 10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$.

**Note:** the copy of this paper available to us stops at question 47. Questions 48 to 50 of the original paper are not included.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.corrige_markdown: A scalar has magnitude only; a vector has magnitude and direction. Force, momentum and displacement are all vectors. Pressure ($p = F/A$) has a size but no direction, so it is a scalar. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following energy conversions takes place when we use an electric iron?
questions.corrige_markdown: The electric current flows through the heating element of the iron, which becomes hot. Electrical energy is converted into heat energy. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A soldier who fires a bullet from a gun has the tendency to move backwards as the bullet flies forward. This observation can be explained by:
questions.corrige_markdown: Before firing, the total momentum of gun and bullet is zero. After firing, the bullet has momentum forward, so the gun (and the soldier holding it) must have an equal momentum backwards so that the total stays zero. This recoil is explained by the conservation of linear momentum. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The air resistance experienced by a moving car can be reduced by:
questions.corrige_markdown: Air resistance increases as the speed increases, so it is reduced by reducing the speed. Driving at a steady speed does not make the air resistance smaller, and a tarred road affects the friction between the tyres and the road, not the air resistance. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following instruments can be used to measure the excess pressure of a trapped mass of gas?
questions.corrige_markdown: A manometer (U-tube containing a liquid) compares the pressure of a trapped gas with the atmosphere and so gives the excess pressure. A barometer measures atmospheric pressure, a thermometer measures temperature and a hygrometer measures humidity. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A body falling in air experiences terminal velocity when its:
questions.corrige_markdown: As the body speeds up, air resistance grows until it equals the weight. The resultant force is then zero, so the acceleration is zero and the body falls at a constant (maximum) velocity. The velocity is not zero and the weight does not disappear. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: velocity decreases at a constant rate

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following surfaces absorbs heat best?
questions.corrige_markdown: Dull black surfaces are the best absorbers (and the best emitters) of thermal radiation. Shiny and white surfaces reflect most of the radiation falling on them. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A liquid-in-glass thermometer is graduated in mm instead of degrees Celsius. The interval between the lower fixed point ($0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$) and the upper fixed point ($100\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$) is $150\ \mathrm{mm}$. When the thermometer is in contact with an unknown liquid the interval between the lower fixed point and the head of the liquid column is $15\ \mathrm{mm}$. The temperature of the unknown liquid is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The length of the column is proportional to the temperature: $\theta = \frac{15}{150}\times 100\,^\circ\mathrm{C} = 10\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$. A common mistake is to read the 15 mm as 15 degrees. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these can be used as a rectifier in electronic circuits?
questions.corrige_markdown: A rectifier changes alternating current into direct current. A diode conducts in one direction only, so it blocks half of each a.c. cycle and rectifies the current. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The image of an object produced by a diverging (concave) lens is always:
questions.corrige_markdown: A diverging lens spreads the rays out, so they never meet: the image is always virtual (on the same side as the object), upright (erect) and smaller (diminished) than the object. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The acceleration due to gravity on earth is $10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ while on the moon it is $1.6\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. If a person whose weight on earth is $500\ \mathrm{N}$ goes to the moon. His weight on the moon will be:
questions.corrige_markdown: The mass is the same everywhere: $m = \frac{W}{g} = \frac{500}{10} = 50\ \mathrm{kg}$. On the moon, $W = mg = 50\times 1.6 = 80\ \mathrm{N}$. Option D confuses weight with mass: the weight changes, the mass does not. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these is a very important property for a liquid used in a liquid-in-glass thermometer?
questions.corrige_markdown: A uniform scale (equal divisions for equal temperature changes) is only possible if the liquid expands in direct proportion to the temperature, that is, linearly. Sensitivity to small changes and a good boiling range are also helpful, but linear expansion is the property that makes the thermometer reliable to read. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Its volume should change linearly with temperature
Its volume should change for small changes in temperature
It should have a high boiling point
It should be a good conductor of heat

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these statements is true for an intrinsic semiconductor?
questions.corrige_markdown: An intrinsic semiconductor is a pure semiconductor. Each electron that is freed by thermal energy leaves behind a hole, so the number of free electrons equals the number of holes. Having more holes than electrons describes a p-type (doped) semiconductor. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: It has some impurities at high temperatures
It has more holes than free electrons
It has equal number of holes as free electrons
It has no impurities and no holes at high temperatures.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following pairs of forces are both contact forces?
questions.corrige_markdown: A contact force acts only when two bodies touch. Friction (surface on surface) and upthrust (fluid on the immersed body) both need contact. Weight, electrostatic force and magnetic force act at a distance (field forces), which eliminates B, C and D. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Water was fetched from a tap and heated till it boiled. Which of the graphs in figure 1 represents the variation of temperature (Y) with time (X) for the water?

![fig-1](gce-ol-physics-2019-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

*Figure 1*
questions.corrige_markdown: Tap water starts at a temperature above $0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ (room temperature or so). The temperature then rises steadily while the water is heated and stays constant at the boiling point ($100\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$) while it boils. Only graph D starts above the origin, rises, then levels off. Graph A also rises then levels off but starts at $0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, which is the temperature of ice, not of tap water. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The unit of pressure is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Pressure $= \frac{\text{force}}{\text{area}}$, measured in newtons per square metre ($\mathrm{N\,m^{-2}}$), which is called the pascal (Pa). Newton metre is the unit of moment (or work) and newton per metre is used for spring constant or surface tension. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Birds can perch safely on high tension electric cables without being electrocuted because:
questions.corrige_markdown: Both feet of the bird touch the same wire, so there is almost no potential difference between its feet. Hence only a negligible current passes through its body. The cable itself carries a large current, so C is wrong, and the bird's legs are not insulators. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: the legs of birds are well insulated
very little current flows in high tension cables
Very little current flows through the body of the bird

questions.enonce_markdown: A machine raises a load of $600\ \mathrm{N}$ through a distance of $2.5\ \mathrm{m}$ when an effort of $100\ \mathrm{N}$ moves through a distance of $20\ \mathrm{m}$. The efficiency of this machine is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Work output $= 600\times 2.5 = 1500\ \mathrm{J}$. Work input $= 100\times 20 = 2000\ \mathrm{J}$. Efficiency $= \frac{1500}{2000}\times 100\% = 75\%$. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: If a particle experiences a deflection in a magnetic field, the particle is most likely:
questions.corrige_markdown: A magnetic force acts only on a moving charge, and it is greatest when the velocity is perpendicular to the field. An uncharged particle feels no magnetic force, and a charged particle moving parallel to the field feels no force either. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: charged and moving perpendicularly to the field lines
charged and moving parallel to the field lines
uncharged and moving perpendicularly to the field lines
uncharged and moving parallel to the field lines

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following are both renewable energy sources?
questions.corrige_markdown: A renewable source is replaced as fast as it is used. Wind and solar radiation are both renewable. Crude oil, natural gas and nuclear fuel are non-renewable. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these radioisotopes is used to monitor the functioning of the thyroid gland?
questions.corrige_markdown: The thyroid gland absorbs iodine, so a small dose of radioactive iodine-131 can be tracked to check how the gland works. Carbon-14 is used for dating, phosphorus-32 for plant studies and sodium-24 for tracing blood flow. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The units of specific heat capacity is:
questions.corrige_markdown: From $c = \frac{Q}{m\,\Delta\theta}$, the unit is joule per kilogram per kelvin: $\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$. In option A the division sign together with the negative power would give the wrong unit. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A current of $0.6\ \mathrm{A}$ flows through a point in a circuit for 5 minutes. The quantity of charge that has passed that point is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Convert the time to seconds: $t = 5\times 60 = 300\ \mathrm{s}$. Then $Q = It = 0.6\times 300 = 180\ \mathrm{C}$. Using 5 s directly gives the wrong value $3\ \mathrm{C}$. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: We hear sounds round corners because sound can be easily:
questions.corrige_markdown: Sound waves have long wavelengths (about 0.1 m to several metres), comparable to the size of doorways and obstacles, so they spread out (diffract) round corners. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Cloud chamber tracks for alpha particles are thick and straight because alpha particles:
questions.corrige_markdown: An alpha particle is heavy, so it is hardly deflected and travels in a straight line. It is also strongly ionizing, producing many ions along its path, which gives a thick, dense track. The other options are true statements about alpha particles but do not explain the thick, straight track. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An object of mass $50\ \mathrm{kg}$ is pulled with a force of $100\ \mathrm{N}$ on a smooth runway. Its acceleration is:
questions.corrige_markdown: A smooth runway means no friction, so the resultant force is $100\ \mathrm{N}$. $a = \frac{F}{m} = \frac{100}{50} = 2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. Option D comes from inverting the formula ($m/F$). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the graphs in figure 2 best represents the variation of count rate (Y) of a radioactive substance with time (X)?

![fig-2](gce-ol-physics-2019-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)

*Figure 2*
questions.corrige_markdown: The count rate is proportional to the number of undecayed nuclei, which falls by half in each half-life. The graph is therefore a decreasing exponential curve that never quite reaches zero: graph D. Graph A shows growth, B a steady rise and C a constant rate. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: On a hydraulic jack a force of $60\ \mathrm{N}$ is applied on the smaller piston with area $0.05\ \mathrm{m^2}$. The force exerted on the larger piston with area $0.6\ \mathrm{m^2}$ will be:
questions.corrige_markdown: The pressure is the same in both pistons: $\frac{F_1}{A_1} = \frac{F_2}{A_2}$. So $F_2 = F_1\times\frac{A_2}{A_1} = 60\times\frac{0.6}{0.05} = 60\times 12 = 720\ \mathrm{N}$. The larger piston gives the larger force. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the graphs in figure 3 best represents the variation of acceleration (Y) of a small ball dropped from the first floor of a storey building with time (x)?

![fig-3](gce-ol-physics-2019-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)

*Figure 3*
questions.corrige_markdown: A small dense ball falling a short distance is in free fall: its acceleration is constant (about $10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$) the whole time. The acceleration-time graph is a horizontal straight line: graph C. Graph B would be the velocity-time graph. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An atom is represented by $^{17}_{8}X$. Which of the nuclides below is an isotope of this atom?
questions.corrige_markdown: Isotopes have the same number of protons (same atomic number, here 8) but different numbers of neutrons (different mass number). $^{16}_{8}X$ has $Z = 8$ and $A = 16$, whereas the atom shown has $A = 17$. The nuclides with $Z = 9$ or $Z = 7$ are different elements. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A transformer has 3000 turns in the primary coil and 500 turns in the secondary coil. If the input voltage is $240\ \mathrm{V}$, the output voltage is:
questions.corrige_markdown: $\frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p}$, so $V_s = 240\times\frac{500}{3000} = 40\ \mathrm{V}$. This is a step-down transformer. Option B comes from inverting the turns ratio. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these electromagnetic waves has the longest wavelength?
questions.corrige_markdown: In the electromagnetic spectrum the wavelength increases in the order gamma rays, X-rays, visible light, infrared. Of the four given, infrared has the longest wavelength. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Water for tea is heated in a pot. Heat is transferred from the bottom of the pot into the pot by method of:
questions.corrige_markdown: The flame heats the metal of the pot. Heat passes through the solid metal, from particle to particle, without the metal itself moving: this is conduction. (Convection occurs afterwards inside the water, but the question asks about the pot itself.) Combustion is a chemical reaction, not a method of heat transfer. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Total internal reflection can only occur when the:
questions.corrige_markdown: Total internal reflection needs light travelling from a denser medium towards a less dense one, with an angle of incidence greater than the critical angle. Then no light is refracted out and all of it is reflected back. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: angle of incidence in the denser medium is less than the critical angle
angle of incidence in the denser medium is greater than the critical angle
angle of incidence in the less dense medium is greater than the critical angle
angle of incidence in the less dense medium is less than the critical angle

questions.enonce_markdown: The activity of a radioactive sample drops from 800 counts/second to 200 counts/second in 24 hours. The half-life of the sample is:
questions.corrige_markdown: $800 \to 400 \to 200$: the activity has halved twice, so 24 hours is 2 half-lives. $T_{1/2} = \frac{24}{2} = 12$ hours. (8 hours would correspond to 3 half-lives.) **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following materials can be used to make the needle of a navigation compass?
questions.corrige_markdown: A compass needle must be a permanent magnet, which needs a material that keeps its magnetism. Steel does. Soft iron is magnetized easily but loses its magnetism just as easily, and zinc and aluminium are not magnetic materials. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: "The EMF induced across a coil acts such as to oppose the change that produces it." This is a statement of:
questions.corrige_markdown: Lenz's law says that the induced EMF acts in the direction that opposes the change producing it. Faraday's law gives the size of the induced EMF; Ohm's law and Hooke's law concern other topics. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The neutron to proton ratio for $^{131}_{54}I$ is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Using the numbers printed in the question: protons $= Z = 54$ and neutrons $= A - Z = 131 - 54 = 77$. The ratio neutrons : protons is $77 : 54$. (The real atomic number of iodine is 53, but the question prints 54 and option B matches those values.) **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A freely suspended bar magnet comes to rest in an approximately north-south direction. This shows that the:
questions.corrige_markdown: The magnet lines up along the field lines of the earth's magnetic field, so the earth must have a magnetic field. Using the earth as a compass is only a consequence, not what the observation shows directly. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: earth can be used as a compass

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the graphs in figure 4 best represents the variation of pressure on an object immersed in a liquid (Y) and the depth of the object (X)?

![fig-4](gce-ol-physics-2019-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.png)

*Figure 4*
questions.corrige_markdown: The pressure in a liquid is $p = h\rho g$, so it is directly proportional to the depth $h$. The graph is a straight line through the origin: graph B. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A body is said to be in mechanical equilibrium when the:
questions.corrige_markdown: A body is in equilibrium when it has no tendency to accelerate or to rotate: the resultant force must be zero AND the resultant moment must be zero. Each of the other options gives only one condition, or a special case. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Resultant external force on it is zero and sum of moments is zero
Sum of external forces on it is zero
Weight is equal to reaction force
Resultant moment on the body is zero.

questions.enonce_markdown: A soft magnetic material is one which:
questions.corrige_markdown: Soft magnetic materials (such as soft iron) are magnetized easily and lose their magnetism easily, so they are used in electromagnets and transformer cores. A material that is magnetized with difficulty but keeps its magnetism (steel) is a hard magnetic material. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: cannot be easily magnetized and demagnetized
can be easily magnetized and easily demagnetized
can be easily magnetized but not easily demagnetized
cannot be easily magnetized but easily demagnetized

questions.enonce_markdown: A temperature of $27\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ converted to kelvin gives:
questions.corrige_markdown: $T(\mathrm{K}) = \theta(^\circ\mathrm{C}) + 273 = 27 + 273 = 300\ \mathrm{K}$. Subtracting instead of adding gives the wrong value $246\ \mathrm{K}$. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The setup in figure 5 is used to study the relationship between current ($I$) and potential difference ($V$) for a wire X.

![fig-5](gce-ol-physics-2019-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_5.png)

*Figure 5*

The ammeter is connected as shown because it has a:
questions.corrige_markdown: In figure 5 the ammeter is in series with the wire X, so the current flows through it. To measure the current without changing it, an ammeter must have a very low resistance. (A very high resistance is what a voltmeter has, and it is connected in parallel.) **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: very high resistance and so allows little current to flow through it
very high resistance and so allows high current to flow through it
very low resistance and so does not alter the current flowing through it
very low resistance and so alters the current flowing through it

questions.enonce_markdown:
The setup in figure 5 is used to study the relationship between current ($I$) and potential difference ($V$) for a wire X.

![fig-5](gce-ol-physics-2019-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_5.png)

*Figure 5*

If the material X is a copper wire, the relationship between V and I when the switch S is closed at constant temperature is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Ohm's law states that for a metallic conductor at constant temperature the potential difference across it is directly proportional to the current through it ($V \propto I$). Hooke's law is about springs, Lenz's rule about induced EMF and Coulomb's law about electric charges. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The setup in figure 5 is used to study the relationship between current ($I$) and potential difference ($V$) for a wire X.

![fig-5](gce-ol-physics-2019-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_5.png)

*Figure 5*

The rheostat, Y is used to:
questions.corrige_markdown: The rheostat is a variable resistor connected in series with the wire. Changing its resistance changes the current in the circuit, which allows several pairs of readings of $V$ and $I$ to be taken. It does not change the resistance of the wire X or the EMF of the cell. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: vary the resistance of the wire
vary the current in the circuit

questions.enonce_markdown:
The most likely shape of the graph of the potential difference (Y) against current (X) for the copper wire in figure 6 is:

![fig-6](gce-ol-physics-2019-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_6.png)

*Figure 6*
questions.corrige_markdown: For the copper wire at constant temperature $V = IR$ with constant $R$: $V$ is directly proportional to $I$, so the graph is a straight line through the origin with gradient $R$: graph B. A curve (A) would show a resistance that changes, as in a filament lamp. **Answer: B.**
